sentences.text:
Rajdeep Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Another on
9 May, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:21957
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal
 On The 9 th Of May, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 44403 of 2024
 Rajdeep Singh
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Another And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Datt - Senior Advocate with Shri Rohit Shar
 the applicant.
Ms. Garima Tiwari - P.L for the respondent/State.

Order 
This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.798/2023 registered at Police Station - Damoh Dehat, District Damoh (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC and 5(j)
(ii)/5(l)/6 of POCSO Act.

Applicant is in detention since 25.12.2023.
2.
As per the prosecution story, in short, is that the present applicant has by way of inducement taken away the minor prosecutrix and committed rape upon her.
She became pregnant, thereafter he threatened her and switched off his mobile.
On the basis of aforesaid, Police registered the case against the present applicant under the aforesaid Sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is in jail since 25.12.2023.
He has been falsely implicated .
It is further submitted that one case being crime no.794/23 under section 317 has been registered against the prosecutrix in which it is mentioned that prosecutrix is minor.
FIR has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21957 2 MCRC-44403-2024 lodged belatedly.
It is further submitted that age of the prosecutrix is not proved as per legal evidence.
In this regard, learned counsel has drawn attention of this Court towards the statement of Mahendra Singh Thakur (P.W-5), Chandrakumar Dubey (P.W-6) and father of the prosecutrix (P.W-13).
He further submitted that prosecutrix was a consenting party and in support of his submission, he has drawn attention of this Court towards the statement of prosecutrix.
Charge sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: There is no criminal record of the applicant.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that applicant threatened the prosecutrix and committed rape with the prosecutrix due to which she got pregnant and delivered a child.
Prosecutrix is minor.
DNA report of the child matched with the applicant.
It is also submitted that minute appreciation of evidence cannot be done at this stage.
This is the second bail application of the applicant.
His earlier application was dismissed on merits.
Hence, he prayed for rejection of bail application.
5. Looking to the overall facts and circumstance of the case, I am not inclined to grant him bail.
Accordingly, the application is dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE anu Rajdeep Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Another on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150662837/
